A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ArgSum study. Their complete main texts, appendices A–E, equations, tables, and figures support comparison, including matching relocated and renamed content.

before.justification: V3 reports original system evaluations on ArgKP21 and Debate, human judgments of 126 generated summaries, and correlations between automatic metrics and those judgments.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and human-evaluation results, with revised system-result entries and additional qualitative examples.

M1.justification: V4 presents standalone end-to-end summarization in Section 3.4 and Figure 2, using the unchanged summary-generation prompt from Appendix B.1. V3 says these summaries undergo further BarH/SMatchToPr processing, whereas v4 depicts direct output. The PDFs do not resolve whether computation changed or the earlier description was corrected. MCArgSum and the evaluation algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ArgQ for quality scoring, ArgKP21 for matching and evaluation, and Debate for additional evaluation. The tasks, represented domains, and human-evaluation coverage remain unchanged; the added qualitative examples concern retained coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 8 replace separate BarH+summ and SMtPR+summ comparisons with one end-to-end entry per already-used LLM. Original systems, candidate-generation variants, clustering systems, and evaluation-metric comparators remain. This is a limited reorganization of the reported comparison set.

E3.justification: The stated evaluation protocols remain unchanged: Appendix D retains preprocessing yielding 428 ArgKP21 and 1165 Debate arguments, the same hyperparameter searches, and the same hardware. Section 4.2 retains the coverage weight of 2/3 and selection and averaging of the best scores within topics and stances.

E4.justification: V4 adds Table 9 with contrasting LLaMA, Qwen3, and GPT-4o outputs on government regulation of social media, extending the existing qualitative examination of summary style. It also expands runtime comparisons. The temperature and matching-threshold sensitivity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions average ten LLM evaluation runs, report the same within-topic correlation standard deviations, and use the same four-annotator agreement procedure. The agreement heatmaps are retained as Figure 2 in v3 and Figure 5 in v4; no new uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: The summary-generation entries are replaced: Qwen3's BarH+summ and SMtPR+summ weighted scores of 0.925/0.900 and 0.920/0.898 become an end-to-end entry of 0.923/0.899 for ArgKP21/Debate. Other retained system scores and metric correlations are unchanged. MCArgSum's reported Debate runtime changes from 7.375 to 7.77 seconds, and v4 adds runtime and example-output results. These replacements do not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same Soft-Precision, Soft-Recall, Coverage-Score, and Weighted Score definitions. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The headline system contribution is redefined from one new system, MCArgSum, to two new systems including end-to-end summarization. V4's conclusion identifies end-to-end summarization as best on both datasets and positions MCArgSum as second on Debate but generally faster. The central evaluation-metric and Qwen3 findings remain.

C2.justification: V4 questions whether traditional multicomponent ArgSum systems remain necessary given end-to-end performance. It also softens the explanation of LLaMA's poor results from attribution to short summaries to a possible attribution. The contamination, prompt-design, and human-evaluation limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 adds an explicit code-and-data access link in the introduction and expands SMatchToPr's candidate-filtering description. It drops v3's explicit BarH token cutoff of 12 without stating a replacement value. Appendix training details, prompts, preprocessing instructions, and hardware specifications otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 modestly changes positioning by promoting standalone prompting as a second novel system and questioning the continued need for traditional ArgSum pipelines. The related-work survey and cited-work membership remain unchanged; the PromptOptMe publication update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: V4 adds a dedicated end-to-end subsection and acknowledgments, expands baseline descriptions, revises the results and conclusion, and standardizes evaluation terminology. Most prose, section ordering, and appendix explanations remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds three substantial system/evaluation diagrams as Figures 2–4, redraws Figure 1 without importance markers, restructures Tables 2 and 8 into three system families, and adds Table 9. The existing agreement heatmap is retained and renumbered. These substantially expand the paper's visual explanation.

improvement.justification: V4 improves accessibility through explanatory diagrams, additional example outputs, and a code-and-data link, while making the LLaMA mechanism explanation more cautious. The experimental evidence remains largely stable. The unexplained relationship between the earlier +summ comparisons and the end-to-end entries limits the gains in methodological clarity and support for the expanded novelty claim.
